structured.description: An export function `createHost` that returns a Language Service Host for TypeScript compilation. The host provides functions for reading files, determining if a file exists, and resolving module names. The code also includes a normalization function `normalize` to modify file names as needed.

items.description: Creates a Language Service Host object that provides file-related functionality for TypeScript compilation, including reading files, resolving module names, and getting script snapshots.

params.name: fileNames
params.description: Used to pass in an array of file names to be processed by the language service host.

params.name: compilerOptions
params.description: Used to provide options for the TypeScript compiler.

params.description: Used to store file metadata, including file names and versions.

params.name: ts
params.description: Used to access the Language Service Host API, which provides methods for resolving module names, reading files, and other language-related functionality.

returns.description: An object that provides various methods for resolving module names, reading files, and getting script snapshots.

items.description: Reads a file synchronously and returns its contents as a string or undefined on error.

params.name: fileName
params.description: Used to represent the name of the file to be read.

params.name: encoding
params.description: Used to specify the encoding of the file content.

returns.description: The contents of the file specified by the `fileName` parameter or undefined if an error occurs while reading the file.

items.name: readFile

params.name: filePath
params.description: Used to specify the path to the file that needs to be read.

returns.description: The contents of the file at the specified path, or a fallback value if the file does not exist or cannot be read.

items.description: Retrieves file content from a file entry and returns it as text. If the file exists, it uses the file's script snapshot to retrieve the content. Otherwise, it falls back to reading the file using a different method.
items.name: readFile

items.description: Maps each input `moduleName` to a resolved module object or undefined, taking into account whether the name ends with `.vue$`. If it does, it returns a custom resolved module object; otherwise, it resolves the module using TypeScript's `ts.resolveModuleName` method and returns the resulting resolved module object.

params.name: moduleNames
params.description: Used to provide a list of module names to resolve.

params.name: containingFile
params.description: Passed as an argument to help identify the file where the modules are being resolved, which allows the function to correctly determine the module resolution.
Not used or mentioned again in the code snippet provided, so its purpose is unknown or unspecified.
Used to store the result of the module resolution process.

params.name: options
params.description: Used to customize the module resolution process.

returns.description: An array of resolved module names.

items.name: resolveModuleNames

items.description: Maps a list of module names to their resolved modules. If a module name ends with ".vue", it returns a custom resolved module object with the file path normalized and resolved. Otherwise, it invokes the `ts.resolveModuleName()` method to retrieve the resolved module information for the given module name.
Normalizes a given file name by replacing the file extension `.vue$` with `.ts`, if the file name matches the pattern `/.vue$/.test(fileName)`. Otherwise, it returns the original file name unchanged.

params.name: fileName
params.description: Intended to represent the file name to be normalized, which may or may not end with the `.vue` suffix.

returns.description: Either the original file name or the modified file name with the extension changed to ".ts" if the file name ends with ".vue$".
